title: Retained issue inventory
caption: Bibliographic and checksum locators for all retained issues.

title: The retained issues by year
caption: Glyphs place every retained issue under its recorded year. Fill identifies the front type, a diagonal marks a separately sourced publisher image, and a red outline marks an open original print scope.
alt: A year-labeled chronological atlas of 281 synthetic issue-front glyphs. Eleven red outlines identify open original print scopes.

title: How text becomes searchable
caption: Thin columns show each retained PDF in chronological issue order. The era bars give each physical page equal weight. The two views distinguish native text, OCR-only text and no admitted text.
alt: Chronological stacks and five era summaries show 7,102 native pages, 2,539 OCR-only pages, and 19 without admitted text.

title: Four patterns of page layout
caption: These common-scale maps show twelve by seventeen cells from each study-authored aggregate raster. Group sizes and issue-weighted shares describe retained page appearance.
alt: Four coarse grayscale layout maps. The largest group contains 8,865 pages and 92.8 percent of issue-normalized weight.

title: What the evidence covers
caption: Each bar names its denominator. Page measurements, exact issue censuses and the distinct complete-appraisal register answer different coverage questions.
alt: Visual measurements cover all 9,660 retained pages. Exact censuses cover 270 of 281 retained issue scopes and 148 of 158 priority scopes. Eleven original print scopes remain open.

title: Native sensitivity and historical OCR contrasts
caption: Shown fixed examples use smoothed log2 ratios of catalog-issued early to late token rates. Lines are marginal 95% diagnostics from 999 whole-issue resamples within each distinct view. No across-view difference or historical cause is inferred.
alt: Seven issue-cluster interval estimates for security and agile, with the cohort sizes listed for each source view.

title: The archive changes the topic map
caption: Matching-page fractions give each PDF equal weight. The early delivery and process example compares native and admitted text under two weightings. The recent intelligent-systems interval shows the effect of resampling represented years.
alt: A nine-family, four-period topic heatmap with a weighting reversal panel and an intelligent-systems year-block interval.

title: Which words carry the topic map?
caption: Each bar shows the fraction of a family rate lost after removing its most influential phrase. The examples show a change in the period-specific leading process phrase and the intelligent-systems rates with and without artificial intelligence.
alt: Nine vocabulary families ordered by the impact of removing one phrase, with separate delivery-process and intelligent-systems examples.

title: Do front-page patterns track the words inside?
caption: The paired symbols compare pooled and centered within-decade and front-role correlations on the same PDFs. The spatial panels show equal-PDF mean per-cell contrasts relative to later pages in each PDF. Red indicates greater darkness and gray indicates less.
alt: Nine paired topic associations with five four-by-four front shape maps.

title: Where full reading reaches
caption: Gray and red points show the fraction in editions 0.20 and 0.21 of native interior pages reached within each literal topic family. The bottom grid compares local nonwhite area on reached and other interior pages from the same strict Calhoun PDF, then gives each eligible PDF equal weight.
alt: Nine before-and-after topic coverage fractions and a 16-cell average within-PDF contrast.

title: A preview, its publisher links, and the full article
caption: Two CrossTalk works recovered through links in the official archive. Arsenault's typeset pagination and the publisher's online placement record different parts of its history. Spicer's title announcement leads to a full HTML article. The original-format units differ, so the paths trace evidence without a shared extent scale.
alt: Two rows trace evidence from a print preview or announcement to the publisher's HTML and its retained format. Arsenault has three typeset pages and two original GIFs.

title: The publisher directory and feed together index the surviving run
caption: Each filled square identifies a publisher link matched to a retained issue with an exact article scope. The July–August 2017 issue is linked in the feed. The final two outlines mark planned periods whose publication is unverified.
alt: A year by issue-pair matrix shows a full run for 2011 through 2016. Four cells are filled in 2017. The March–April 2011 cell points to a separately appraised online article.

title: How the PASS error count fell
caption: Koester’s Figure 1 as transcribed from the November 1994 publisher reflow and checked against Fairley’s teaching slide. All bars share the same zero-to-123 scale. The separate NASA table uses different categories and reports 124 for OI-23.
alt: Four horizontal bars show 123 errors initially, 31 after inspection, 9 after pre-build work and 2 after independent testing. Detection counts are 92, 22 and 7.

title: Pages and articles in eleven open issues
caption: The eleven open print scopes preserve 197 physical PDF pages and 66 confirmed complete bodies, including three embedded web bodies. The last column records partial bodies and disputed regions where enumerated.
alt: Eleven retained issues have aligned horizontal bars for physical pages and confirmed complete bodies, with a separate pair of partial and disputed counts.

title: Exact wording across two 1992 versions
caption: Alignment of the four March 1992 journal pages against twelve thesis appendix pages. The bar counts the union of OCR word positions in page-bounded exact blocks at least eight words long. The sequence profile counts distinct contiguous word windows observed in both sources. These are lexical measures under the stated transcription and matching rule.
alt: 2,254 of 2,993 journal OCR positions align in qualifying blocks (75.31%). The longest block is 119 words. Both texts share 424 distinct 50-word sequences.
